transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-10-19
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 49 minutes
Recording: fireflies transcript
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Jamie (Redwood SE), Sana (Redwood SE), Priya (ACME CTO), Carlos (ACME ML Eng), Emma (ACME PM)

Summary:
Short demo focused on Redwood's structured output / JSON mode with function/tool calling. Walked through API examples, Console mapping schemas, and Optimize recommendations for batching/quantization. Discussed security (KMS, SOC2) and pilot scope (1-week benchmark).

Topics:
- JSON/structured-output mode and schema enforcement
- Function/tool calling integration and guardrails
- Console flow for mapping and validation
- Redwood Optimize for cost/latency tradeoffs
- Security: KMS, audit logs, VPC/Private deployment considerations

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick roll call?
[00:05] Priya (CTO): Hi, Priya here. Got Carlos and Emma with me.
[00:09] Alex (AE): Awesome. Jamie, you want to intro?
[00:12] Jamie (SE): Yeah, hi all, Jamie Lin on the solutions eng side \u2014 I'll do the deep part of the demo, focus on the JSON schema enforcement and function calling.
[00:20] Emma (PM): Thanks, looking forward. We want to see how reliably it can output structured inventory updates and call our downstream pricing tool.
[00:30] Jamie (SE): Great. Quick agenda: API example -> Console mapping -> function-calling -> guardrails/validation -> Optimize recommendations and pilot plan.
[00:40] Alex (AE): And we'll cover security and next steps at the end.

[02:15] Jamie (SE): Okay jumping into the API \u2014 here's a standard text-generation call but we set response_format: json and provide a schema. So for your inventory example we'll validate fields: sku, quantity, price_cents, store_location. If the model doesn't match the schema, Redwood can either coerce, reject, or return a structured error depending on the policy.
[02:42] Carlos (ML Eng): Quick q, how strict is the validation? We need numbers not strings, and enums for location.
[02:50] Jamie (SE): Good q. You pick strictness. In Console you can set strictTypes=true which will reject mismatches, or you can set a best-effort coercion. For pilot I'd recommend strict + fallback pathway so you catch regressions.
[03:10] Priya (CTO): And example errors surface in the trace? We need auditability for legal.
[03:18] Sana (SE): Yes, every rejected output is logged with request/response, token counts, and the failing validation path. Those logs are part of the audit trail and can be exported to your SIEM.

[05:05] Jamie (SE): Now function calling \u2014 you can register a function like update_inventory(sku, quantity, price_cents, store) and Redwood will map the model output to that function. We demoed a sample where the model returns a JSON payload and we call your webhook.
[05:30] Emma (PM): How do we prevent the model from calling sensitive functions or returning fabricated skus?
[05:36] Jamie (SE): Two layers: schema enforcement (prevents malformed fields) and guardrails \u2014 you can whitelist functions per route, and Redwood's policy can block unknown skus by validating against your catalog via a small synchronous lookup or cache. There's a KV cache option but sometimes folks call it key-v cash in docs, we had a typo earlier, lol.
[06:10] Carlos (ML Eng): About latency \u2014 function calling adds an extra hop. If we have a 200ms model response and 100ms webhook, that's bad for user experience. Options?
[06:20] Jamie (SE): Right \u2014 you can do two patterns: synchronous call where Redwood calls your webhook inline (adds that webhook latency), or return the structured payload to the app and let it call your service async. For low-latency paths we recommend returning JSON and having the app handle the call or using a small Dedicated endpoint with colocated services to minimize network hops.

[08:05] Alex (AE): Quick pause \u2014 competitors? Priya asked earlier if you evaluated others.
[08:12] Priya (CTO): We looked at OpenAI and Anthropic; curious about model provenance and deployed model variants.
[08:19] Alex (AE): Redwood provides a model catalog with verified profiles and you can pin model versions. For Dedicated/Private we can seed with the model you choose and we surface performance profiles in the Console.

[10:30] Jamie (SE): Switching to Console \u2014 here's the mapping UI. You upload a JSON schema or draw fields inline, set required vs optional, types, and set validation behavior. Then you can preview model outputs against a sample prompt set.
[11:02] Emma (PM): Can we add transformation rules? Like price_cents = round(price_float * 100)?
[11:10] Jamie (SE): Yup \u2014 Console has post-process transforms and also can call a transform function (sandboxed). For heavier logic you do it in your service after receiving the structured payload.

[13:40] Jamie (SE): Guardrails: you can add sanity-check rules (e.g., quantity >=0, price_cents < 1000000) and have failing rules route to manual review queue. Those are surfaced in the Rollouts page in the Console.
[14:05] Carlos (ML Eng): For the pilot we'd like to test regression detection \u2014 is that automatic?
[14:12] Sana (SE): Redwood Optimize ties into eval sets \u2014 you can seed a prompt set and expected schema outputs; we run nightly sample checks and surface quality regression alerts if the pass rate drops.

[16:00] Jamie (SE): Quick demo of function calling with toolchain: model proposes an update, we simulate the webhook which checks the SKU against a small catalog and returns accept/reject. In the example, if SKU unknown we return a structured error and Redwood logs it as a validation failure.
[16:30] Priya (CTO): If it rejects, can we run an automated fallback to a human-in-the-loop?
[16:36] Jamie (SE): Yes \u2014 fallback policies support canary -> human-in-loop -> queued retry. You control the policy per-route.

[19:20] Alex (AE): Security checklist time \u2014 Priya, you mentioned SOC2 and KMS. We have SOC2 Type II report and integrate with customer KMS for private deployments.
[19:36] Priya (CTO): Can we rotate keys via our HSM?
[19:40] Sana (SE): We can integrate with your HSM for on-prem or VPC deployments; key rotation policies are supported and we log key access. We'll send the security pack after this call.

[22:55] Carlos (ML Eng): Benchmarks \u2014 we'll want per-token cost numbers and tail latency for 95th pct. Can Redwood produce those for our prompt distribution?
[23:05] Jamie (SE): Yes \u2014 we run a sample bench using your prompt set and produce per-route token breakdowns, 50/95/99 latencies, and cost estimates for hosted vs dedicated vs local quantized variants. We'll include the spreadsheet.

[26:40] Jamie (SE): On Optimizations: for your high-throughput inventory updates, we recommend prefix caching for repeated product chunks, batching small updates into a single call with Redwood's continuous batching, and considering an int8 quantized model on Dedicated to reduce cost.
[26:58] Carlos (ML Eng): Any caveats with quantization and structured output accuracy?
[27:05] Jamie (SE): Tradeoffs exist \u2014 quantization can slightly affect token-level accuracy. Optimize will run A/B against your evals and recommend when accuracy drop is within acceptable bounds vs cost savings.

[30:00] Emma (PM): Pilot scope?
[30:05] Alex (AE): Proposed: 1-week pilot to run benchmarks against a 5k prompt sample, validate schema pass rate > 98%, measure 95th latency, and test function-calling integration against a sandbox webhook. We'll provide a benchmark script and pricing for a short Reserved window if you want Dedicated trial.
[30:25] Priya (CTO): Sounds good. Timeline: want pilot next week if possible.
[30:30] Alex (AE): We'll target kickoff 2027-10-25 pending your OK and stakeholder list.

[32:50] Jamie (SE): Quick gotcha \u2014 sometimes names and acronyms get mangled in transcriptions, e.g., KV cache shown as key-v cache; just flagging that logs may have small noise.
[33:10] Carlos (ML Eng): Ha that's fine. Also curious about costs for high-volume \u2014 is there burst capacity?
[33:18] Alex (AE): Yes dedicated has burst options; we can model your load and show projected costs for different commit levels.

[35:00] Emma (PM): Onboarding friction \u2014 who needs to be involved for pilot?
[35:05] Alex (AE): Typically we need an eng owner (Carlos), a product owner (Emma) and an infra/security contact (Priya). We'll also loop in the solutions team (Jamie, Sana).

[37:45] Priya (CTO): About data residency \u2014 we may need EU-only. Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem \u2014 what's the effort?
[37:55] Sana (SE): For VPC Private we can spin up a control plane in region and connect to your VPC; on-prem is slightly longer lead time but doable. We'll include deployment timelines in the security pack.

[40:10] Jamie (SE): Demo wrap: showed sample code for API call (response_format: json, schema id) and Console mapping screenshots. Shared deck link in chat: https://redwood.ai/deck/structured-output-demo (note: link shorthand). Also sent benchmark spreadsheet template: /s/benchmarks-template.csv

[42:30] Alex (AE): Recap of next steps \u2014 we will: send pricing + Dedicated vs Hosted comparison, security whitepaper + SOC2, benchmark script and sample prompt set, and schedule pilot kickoff 2027-10-25.

[44:00] Priya (CTO): Thanks all, we'll review and confirm stakeholder list.

[44:10] Carlos (ML Eng): I'll prepare the 5k prompt sample and share credentials for sandbox webhook.

[46:20] Emma (PM): One last question \u2014 can Redwood's Console export a CI-friendly JSON for our pipeline?
[46:28] Jamie (SE): Yep you can export mappings and validation rules as JSON and commit them to your repo as part of infra-as-code.

[48:00] Alex (AE): Thanks everyone \u2014 we'll follow up in email.

End of recording.
